Subject: Follow-up: KMS & encryption questions + vendor questionnaire

Hi Sara — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II in production; attached is a high-level SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). We can provide the full report under an NDA/SoW if needed.
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2/1.3 by default between clients and our hosted endpoints; mutual TLS available for Dedicated/private deployments.
- Data at rest: Customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. For hosted API, by default keys are managed by the cloud provider and Redwood.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments. With CMKs you can rotate and revoke keys; we support envelope encryption where the data key encrypts model artifacts and KV caches.

Questions I noted from the call you wanted answers for:
1) Can FinBank bring its own KMS/HSM and have redwood use it for at-rest encryption?
2) Are there any limitations to using CMKs with streaming or caching features?
3) What evidence do you need for procurement (SOC 2, encryption diagrams, SLA)?

Next steps I propose:
- I attached our high-level KMS diagram and the questionnaire you shared (FinBank_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). Please confirm which specific sections you want us to complete first — usually customers start with encryption/KMS and network/security controls.
- I'll loop in Aditya (solutions engineer) to provide a short tech note on CMK integration and HSM options.
- Camila will follow up on procurement and timelines.

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min technical deep dive this week.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Sara — quick technical note from the infra side: 

- Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed keys backed by HSM (CloudHSM) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted deployments we can integrate with your cloud KMS (AWS KMS with CloudHSM-backed CMKs) via an MR (managed key) setup, but there are operational tradeoffs.

- Recommended architecture: envelope encryption. Data keys are generated locally by the Redwood runtime and encrypted with your CMK. Encrypted data keys are stored alongside the data. This minimizes synchronous KMS calls on the hot path — only the envelope key unwrap needs a KMS call (typically at start-up or cache miss). That preserves low-latency streaming.

- For streaming + KV cache: we keep the unencrypted in-memory key material in process for active cache segments; it's never written to disk unencrypted. If you require a strict model where the KMS must be called per-request, performance will degrade. We can support stricter modes for Dedicated/private if required, but we'd like to understand latency SLAs.

- Auditing/logging: when integrated with your KMS, you get KMS-level logs (e.g., AWS CloudTrail events). Redwood can also emit access logs and a key-rotation history to your SIEM via our telemetry hooks.

I'll attach a short diagram and a one-pager about envelope encryption and streaming behavior (redwood-kms-diagram.png). Happy to jump on a 30-min deep dive to walk through specifics and map to your SOC 2 requirements.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
